item.title: EA Sports is using generative AI to create voiceover for its in-game commentators in NHL 27, according to veteran sports commentator John Buccigross.
item.description: EA Sports is using generative AI to create voiceover for its in-game commentators in NHL 27, according to veteran sports commentator John Buccigross. When speaking on the Chirping Zebras podcast (initially spotted by Insider Gaming's Mike Straw), Buccigross was talking about his experience working with EA Sports on the NHL games. He revealed that he will be in NHL 27, but EA also used generative AI to add voice lines as well. "They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," said Buccigross. "It's like 'Wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it. Sometimes AI will get something wrong. One of the guys was playing it back, and a lot of these guys maybe aren't hardcore sports fans; they're video game extrordinares. They're not always up on the vernacular. So they're playing back my AI voice, and they're like, 'Score! And the crowd gets out of their chairs!' I was like, 'No, they're not chairs. They look like chairs, but we call them seats.' "So, little things like that, you gotta go back and listen because words matter. [...] But then you can make AI smarter; in the future they'll say seats, they won't say chairs. You have to manually put that in. That was kind of a funny anecdote from the process."

item.title: If you were upset to hear that pop star Ariana Grande wouldn't return in Final Fantasy Resonance, a new mod is here to save the day.
item.description: If you were upset to hear that pop star Ariana Grande wouldn't return in Final Fantasy Resonance, a new mod is here to save the day. In case you were unaware, Square Enix's Final Fantasy Resonance will arrive as the long-running RPG franchise's first proper HD-2D game when it launches next month, and it also happens to be a bit of a remake. The game it's based on, Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, is a free-to-play game with turn-based gameplay that launched for iOS and Android devices in 2015 and shut down in 2025 – but what does that have to do with Ariana Grande? The performer behind hits like "break up with your girlfriend, i'm bored," who also played Galinda in the recent Wicked films, isn't a newcomer for the Final Fantasy series. Grande actually joined Final Fantasy Brave Exvius in the form of pixelated characters – including one fit with her Dangerous Woman era bunny outfit – in 2017. The announcement (below) even detailed some in-game love for the pop star's song "Touch It," but when it comes to Final Fantasy Resonance, Grande's contribution to the series will be lost to time. Producer Keisuke Nakashima recently confirmed to Kotaku that Grande "unfortunately" would not appear in the October Final Fantasy game. At the very least, it sounds like a decision Square Enix put some thought into.

item.title: The Winter Soldier himself, Sebastian Stan, recently pitched a "Sicario-esque" Bucky Barnes movie to Marvel Studios leadership.
item.description: The Winter Soldier himself, Sebastian Stan, recently pitched a "Sicario-esque" Bucky Barnes movie to Marvel Studios leadership. When speaking to New York Magazine, Stan revealed that he pitched Kevin Feige on a solo Bucky Barnes film in the vein of Denis Villeneuve's 2015 movie, Sicario. The film would have been smaller in scope, with a tighter budget, and focused on a more personal mission for Bucky. Stan noted that he was "half-joking" with his pitch, but Feige responded well to it and said it sounds cool. "We keep a real small budget," said Stan. "It's about a guy who thinks he recognizes someone from his past that had something to do with when, you know, he was brainwashed, and he gets obsessed with this person. He goes on a whole journey to try to figure out who this person is. It's a thriller." Although the MCU is intricately mapped out, the franchise has always had room to add in these kinds of unique passion projects. Ghost Rider, for instance, is something Ryan Gosling personally campaigned for and pitched to Marvel. The vision for the project was strong enough for Gosling to get the green light, and now, he'll make his MCU debut in summer 2028. Whether Stan's passionate about pursuing this idea enough to make it a reality remains to be seen, but joke or not, the idea does sound like it could be a breath of fresh air for the franchise. It would also put a beloved character front and center after being relegated to a supporting character for over a decade.

item.title: Forza Horizon 6 is still planned to launch on PS5 this year, despite not having a firm release date yet.
item.description: Forza Horizon 6 is still planned to launch on PS5 this year, despite not having a firm release date yet. Playground Games has confirmed it still plans to release Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 this year, following rumors that it might be delayed. Nothing else was shared about the port, but the clock is ticking for this new version. "If you’re planning your trip to Discover Japan on PlayStation 5, stay tuned!" Playground said in a post today. "Forza Horizon 6 will be releasing on PS5 later this year, and you can add the game to your Wishlist on the PlayStation Store to be notified of availability." September and October are loaded with big releases like Marvel's Wolverine and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, but there is enough difference in the audiences for these respective titles for Forza Horizon 6 to still succeed. November, however, is a different story. Launching Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 in November seems like a death wish given GTA 6 is set to dominate the industry upon its release. GTA 6 is expected to have an in-depth car customization system and races in addition to all of the other features one expects from GTA, making it hard to imagine players choosing Forza over GTA.

item.title: Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for its own good.
item.description: Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for its own good. We've learned a lot about GTA 6 since its big extended look reveal. While the 13-year wait for Jason and Lucia's story already seems worth it for some, others fear Rockstar has taken its commitment to realistic gameplay a bit too seriously when it comes to its new open-world video game. The studio is known for packing its games with details that fans could spend years combing through – and for better or worse, GTA 6 seems no different. Co-development lead Rob Nelson promised as much during a recent interview with content creator TGG. One element where the new Grand Theft Auto will differ from its predecessor involves how NPCs react to guns, with Nelson teasing that you can't just wander around with an RPG and expect zero pushback. "The reactions are much more nuanced than before," he said. "So, if you've got a long gun on your back, you should be fine. If you've got one in your hand, people don't like it, and they react and start moving away from you. The more guns you carry and the way you carry them matters.

item.title: Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some fans are already planning to adjust their console region and play early.
item.description: Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some fans are already planning to adjust their console region and play early. Rather than offering a fixed time worldwide, the midnight local rollout means players in New Zealand will get a roughly 20-hour headstart on Mexico and elsewhere in Central America. Of course, there are no GTA 6 discs to get started with early — even though Rockstar's long-awaited release will arrive as an entirely single-player experience. While pre-loading will be available, the game itself will not unlock until your timezone's allotted window. Timestamps spotted on the PlayStation Store by GTAVice show 15 major release times for GTA 6 across the world's various timezones, beginning in New Zealand at 11am UTC on November 18, which is midnight on November 19 for our Kiwi friends.

item.title: Lilly Wachowski has said she’s “kinda done” with The Matrix, and suggested the recently announced The Matrix 5 may not move forward without the Wachowski’s blessing.
item.description: Lilly Wachowski has said she’s “kinda done” with The Matrix, and suggested the recently announced The Matrix 5 may not move forward without the Wachowski’s blessing. Warner Bros. announced The Matrix 5 in 2024, with The Martian and The Cabin in the Woods' Drew Goddard on board to write and direct. If it goes ahead, The Matrix 5 will be the first The Matrix movie not to have either Lana or Lilly Wachowski in the directing chair, although Lana Wachowski was reportedly down to executive produce. “Drew came to Warner Bros. with a new idea that we all believe would be an incredible way to continue the Matrix world, by both honoring what Lana and Lilly began over 25-years ago and offering a unique perspective based on his own love of the series and characters," Warner Bros. Motion Pictures President of Production Jesse Ehrman said in a statement issued two years ago. "The entire team at Warner Bros. Discovery is thrilled for Drew to be making this new Matrix film, adding his vision to the cinematic canon the Wachowskis’ spent a quarter of a century building here at the studio.” Fast forward to now, and Lilly Wachowski has poured cold water on excitement around The Matrix 5. “Warner Bros., they wanna make another thing,” she said in an interview on KCRW’s The Business, as reported by Variety. “They’re always gonna wanna make another thing. Personally, I don’t wanna play in that sandbox anymore. I’m kinda done.”

item.title: Capcom looks like it has yet another hit video game on its hands, with Onimusha: Way of the Sword selling over 1 million copies on launch day.
item.description: Capcom looks like it has yet another hit video game on its hands, with Onimusha: Way of the Sword selling over 1 million copies on launch day. The milestone pushed total Onimusha franchise sales over the 10 million units sold mark, 20 years after the last new game in the series came out. “... through several marketing initiatives prior to launch, such as multiple demo releases and hands-on exhibitions, Capcom worked to expand awareness among a broad range of users, resulting in sales surpassing 1 million units on the day of its release,” Capcom said in a statement online. But of most interest here is Capcom’s comment about repeating the Onimusha trick with other games from its back catalog.

item.title: Gary Oldman has said Amazon has finally decided which actor will play the new James Bond, and he’s backing his Slow Horses co-star.
item.description: Gary Oldman has said Amazon has finally decided which actor will play the new James Bond, and he’s backing his Slow Horses co-star. Speaking to Canada’s The Morning Show to promote Slow Horses Season 6, Oldman teased 36-year-old Jack Lowden as Bond. Here’s exactly what Oldman said: “Jack… it’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist, or he’s one of… we’re gonna find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice. But they have not announced it yet. So, my fingers are crossed for Jack.” Does that sound like Oldman is in the know here? Perhaps Jack Lowden let the good news slip during some downtime on-set. Perhaps this is just odd wording from Oldman, and he’s simply backing his colleague and doesn’t actually know. But he does sound convinced that a decision has been made, and an announcement is imminent.

item.title: Tarae: The Unbound developers explain why this South Korean action RPG will stand out from the crowd.
item.description: One of the most impressive games I played at gamescom was Tarae: The Unbound, a new action RPG developed by South Korean studio Boundary and published by PUBG company Krafton. There’s a huge amount here that will feel familiar to fans of Diablo, not least in the way the game actually plays. But it’s how Tarae: The Unbound looks that its developers hope fans of the genre will find something unique. Tarae: The Unbound is based in east Asia between the 15th and 17th centuries (most action RPGs, including Diablo, are set in medieval Europe), and it leans heavily on Eastern aesthetics and folklore to come up with a different take. You can see this in everything from the class design to the monsters you fight and the environments you fight them in. But the boss fights (there are over 80 at launch!) are the best example of this Eastern aesthetic — a mix of Chinese, South Korean, and Japanese influences coming together to form designs I’ve not seen in an action RPG before. As a big fan of Diablo, I was able to settle into Tarae: The Unbound quickly, my fingers resting on the number keys for abilities, my thumb on the space bar for a dodge, and my mouse fingers clicking away to delete mobs via the weighty combat. You can even pull the camera back to get a wider view that presents almost the entire battlefield on-screen, so you can see the waves of enemies coming from a decent distance. There’s a steady stream of loot to fuss over, various skills to pick from, and, of course, build crafting. So far, so very Diablo. But, speaking to Inyoung Koo, CEO of Boundary, art director Byung Ho Park, and creative Myung Sang Ryu in an interview following my hands-on time, I could tell that Boundary feels Tarae: The Unbound has a lot more to offer.

item.title: Mewtwo is being milked too hard, fans say, as Pokémon Go continues to capitalize on the creature's popularity and monetization potential.
item.description: There's a feeling that Mewtwo is being milked too hard, as Pokémon Go continues to capitalize on the creature's popularity and monetization potential. The announcement of yet more Mewtwo coming to Pokémon Go later this year is being greeted with surprising apathy by fans, following a disappointing end of summer event this past weekend marred by yet more technical issues. Mewtwo raids returned to Pokémon Go this summer after an extended absence, fuelling FOMO ahead of the long-awaited Mega Mewtwo X and Y release at Go Fest events in May, June, and July. Mega Mewtwo was also the star of the game's controversial New York anniversary event, disquiet over which preceded all players being gifted a unique 100% stat Mewtwo. Go Fest Global in July, the game's biggest annual event, was essentially a Mega Mewtwo raid weekend for all players, which was fine — except for technical glitches that saw raiding impacted over a series of timezones across the world. A makeup event then took place in late July with more Mega Mewtwo offered.

item.title: Sony is reportedly in the early stages of bringing its first-person shooter series, Killzone, back from the dead.
item.description: Sony is reportedly in the early stages of bringing its first-person shooter series, Killzone, back from the dead. Guerrilla Games’ Halo killer fell by the wayside after the developer found enormous success with Horizon Zero Dawn back in 2017. It has focused on the Horizon franchise ever since, but Killzone retains a loyal following, and fans often call for it to return. According to MP1st, Sony may be working on doing just that, with Bulletstorm and Outriders maker People Can Fly drafted in to co-dev. But what is this new Killzone game? Apparently it’s a Killzone remaster or remake, and while we’re not sure which Killzone is getting a fresh coat of paint, the first Killzone game, released on the PlayStation 2 in 2004, is a safe bet. There’s a lot going on at Guerrilla right now. PlayStation recently rebooted Horizon multiplayer spinoff Hunters Gathering following negative feedback, and, according to MP1st, the studio will move on to Killzone after it’s done doing that. According to Bloomberg, Guerrilla has until December to impress PlayStation bosses with Hunters Gathering’s next milestone, but already some Hunters Gathering staff moved over to another Guerrilla project with a milestone due at the end of this year. Apparently a “tiny team” is working on the next Horizon single-player game, which we’ll call Horizon 3 but will undoubtedly carry a new subtitle, but it’s still years away.

item.title: Nintendo is developing an all-new Super Smash Bros and Nintendogs, a notable leaker has claimed.
item.description: Nintendo is developing an all-new Super Smash Bros and Nintendogs, a notable leaker has claimed. The details come from Malo932, who recently stated that Nintendo would hold two Direct presentations this week (correct), and who previously stated that a classic Star Fox, Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and new Switch Sports would all be announced and launched this year (all correct too). Word of a new Smash Bros. game is enormously exciting to the fighting game series' huge fanbase, though perhaps not a huge surprise considering how well Super Smash Bros. Ultimate sold on Nintendo Switch (at 38 million copies, it is the console's third-best selling game, behind Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Animal Crossing: New Horizons). But one notable detail here is more surprising — that this is a new game, rather than a souped-up version of Ultimate. How the company plans to beat the Switch's hugely ambitious installment remains to be seen. A fresh Nintendogs is another surprise, more than a decade on from Nintendogs + Cats, the franchise's last release back on 3DS in 2011.

item.title: Nicolas Cage has insisted just one season of Spider-Noir is “perfect” after Amazon canceled the Prime video show.
item.description: Nicolas Cage has insisted just one season of Spider-Noir is “perfect” after Amazon canceled the Prime Video show. Spider-Noir sees Cage play Ben Reilly, a down-on-his-luck private investigator and the city's sole super-powered vigilante in 1930s New York City during the Prohibition Era. Season 1 debuted on MGM+ on May 25, 2026, followed by a global release on Prime Video two days later. You can watch Spider-Noir in both black and white, and in color. IGN's Spider-Noir review returned an 8/10. "Nicolas Cage’s Bogie-meets-Bugs Bunny pulp hero invigorates the highly entertaining, genre-bending Spider-Noir," we said. As reported by Deadline, Spider-Noir saw a strong start in terms of viewing minutes, but it fell away soon after launch and dropped out of Prime Video’s top 10 chart. This, coupled with the high cost associated with producing the show, apparently contributed to Amazon’s decision to give it the chop.

item.title: Amazon's canned Stargate reboot would have starred Michael Shanks' fan-favorite character Daniel Jackson, trapped in a parallel universe.
item.description: Amazon's canned Stargate reboot would have starred Michael Shanks' fan-favorite character Daniel Jackson, trapped in a parallel universe. Jackson confirmed he had been involved in the project this weekend at the Starfury: Ascension 2 convention in Birmingham, UK this weekend (thanks, Gateworld) prompting more details on the project to be spilled via prolific Stargate fan podcast Dial the Gate. Those details included the series' proposed setting: an alternate universe where numerous plot elements from past Stargate series would not have occurred. The idea here, it seems, would have been to offer a soft reboot of the franchise's continuity in order to cater for a new audience. At the same time, the franchise's original Daniel Jackson would have been a regular character — giving returning fans a familiar face to tune in for, who still carried the knowledge of the original Stargate universe.

item.title: A24 has released a teaser trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s surprise Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything — and it’s quite something.
item.description: A24 has released a teaser trailer for Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s surprise Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything — and it’s quite something. For the uninitiated, Elizabeth Holmes is currently serving an 11-year prison sentence at the Federal Prison Camp Bryan in Texas for defrauding investors in her blood-testing startup, Theranos. Holmes, who married hotel heir Billy Evans in 2019 and with whom she has had two children (one born in 2021, the other in 2023), began her sentence on May 30, 2023. But 34 days before she was sent to prison, Holmes invited Canadian comedian Nathan Fielder and a film crew into her home to document her every move. The film is the result of this unprecedented access and a three-year journey that certainly goes places, based on reviews to a secret screening on Sunday. This teaser offers just a glimpse of what to expect from the 174-minute documentary, but it’s an intense watch. Fielder and Holmes are extremely close, looking into each other’s eyes as the notorious Silicon Valley founder insists she’s being genuine.

item.title: Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic has patched out a sex mini-game after a gameplay clip went viral. Now, the studio has issued a statement.
item.description: UPDATE: IllFonic has provided IGN with the following statement, confirming the removal of the sex minigame: "Players may have noticed that our latest hotfix removed the Two-Person Power-Up minigame. This was due to an unintended issue that allowed end game reinforcement characters to engage with the minigame, which was a major oversight on our part. We have more content and minigames coming in the near future but current focus is our attention on immediate game needs. Keep an eye on our socials for updates as they become available.” ORIGINAL STORY: Halloween: The Game developer IllFonic appears to have patched out a sex minigame after a gameplay clip went viral. The video game adaptation of the iconic 1970s slasher movie lets players have sex in a closet, but one video of this minigame featuring Samuel Loomis raised eyebrows given the character, who is in his fifties during the events of the game and is based on deceased actor Donald Pleasence’s likeness, can have sex with teenagers.

item.title: Robert Pattinson has suggested The Batman Part 2 will be a very different take on the DC superhero than we’ve seen before.
item.description: Robert Pattinson has suggested The Batman Part 2 will be a very different take on the DC superhero than we’ve seen before. Pattinson is set to reprise his role as the Caped Crusader in The Batman Part 2, which has a February 18, 2028 release date. Assuming it hits that date, Part 2 will arrive in theaters just shy of six years after The Batman came out. The movie is largely shrouded in mystery, but Pattinson has started to tease what to expect from it now he’s out and about promoting his new movie, Primetime. And in an interview captured by MYmovies on TikTok, Pattinson teased something quite different than what’s gone before. “Matt just wrote this amazing script,” Pattinson said of The Batman co-writer and director Matt Reeves. “I think the first one was… it’s difficult to reinvent Batman as this new thing. And then to go in another totally different direction. I’m just looking at the playback on certain things… it looks different to the first one.

item.title: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise.
item.description: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has said he feels like he’s been on an “apology tour” while navigating skepticism from some fans about his movie adaptation of Capcom’s horror franchise. Cregger, director of hugely popular horror movies Barbarian and Weapons, has faced scrutiny from Resident Evil fans ever since it was confirmed that his adaptation wouldn’t feature any characters from the video games, or tell any of the stories already told in the video games. Instead, Cregger has charted his own path, telling a horror story set in the world of Resident Evil that references some of the video games' tropes. In an interview with The Playlist, Cregger outlined how it has felt to promote Resident Evil amid this backlash. “I feel like I’ve been on somewhat of an apology tour,” he said. “I feel like I’m running for office, trying to get these people not to call me a LARPer.”

item.title: Exodus is an upcoming sci-fi RPG that will account for the decisions you make in its story, and its narrative director explains how it'll all be reflected in the end.
item.description: Any time you look at or talk about Exodus, the upcoming space opera RPG from Archetype Entertainment, the Mass Effect comparisons start flying at light speed. I mean, Exodus narrative director Drew Karpyshyn played a major role as a writer and lead at BioWare to shape the stories of its biggest hits. In our conversation following my hands-on preview of Exodus, he told me that Mass Effect is a perfectly fine way for people to wrap their head around what this new game is. The parallels don't end with the Paladin/Immortal morality system or the romance and relationship dynamics that are going to drive the story, either. He hinted at how the decisions you make can impact Exodus' ending. Of course, that's not exclusive to BioWare games by any stretch, but when the Mass Effect 2's suicide mission is regarded as a series pinnacle, no one would blame to draw a quick comparison. When I asked about the relationship systems in Exodus, Karpyshyn emphasized wanting to make them feel real and said it's about, "[M]aking their relationship with you grow, allowing it to evolve from the choices you've made, and realizing that the choices you make are going to bring some companions closer to you, but maybe push some companions farther away." He took it one step further, and told me, "Without spoiling too much, we definitely want to have it impact how their storylines go." Then he took it another step further and concluded, "Depending on choices you make, by the end of the game, you might not have every companion with you that you started with. That's about all I can say!"
